## What is R?

When you collect fisheries data, you need a way to make sense of it: to add up catches,
compare landing sites, or spot a month when something looks wrong. **R is a free tool made
for exactly this.**

Think of R as a careful, very fast assistant. You give it a short written instruction —
*"add up the weight"*, *"show me only the landings from Vanga"* — and it does the work exactly
and straight away, whether you have ten records or one hundred thousand. It is the same tool
used by the scientists who prepare your data.

A spreadsheet like Excel is fine for a small table. R goes further: it does not slow down with
large amounts of data, it does not make copy-and-paste mistakes, and it remembers every step —
so the same work can be repeated next month without starting over.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What is this page, then?

This page runs R **right inside your web browser**. There is nothing to download or install —
it just works, and it is free.

You do **not** need to be a programmer. In these lessons you will mostly **press a button** and
change a few small things. And **you cannot break anything**: if something looks wrong, just
press **Run** again.
:::

## How it works: press Run

Below is a small table of fish landings — just six rows, so it is easy to read.

The first box runs **on its own** when the page opens. (The very first time, the page may take a few
seconds to wake up — that is normal.) Look for the green **▶ Run** button on the box: you can press it
to run the box again.

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
# A small example table: six catches from two landing sites.
landings_example <- data.frame(
  date      = c("2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-06", "2024-01-06", "2024-01-07", "2024-01-07"),
  site      = c("Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Vanga", "Shimoni", "Vanga", "Vanga"),
  fish      = c("Tilapia", "Snapper", "Tilapia", "Octopus", "Snapper", "Tilapia"),
  weight_kg = c(12, 5, 8, 3, 6, 10)
)

landings_example
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**What you should see:** a table with **6 rows** and **4 columns** — `date`, `site`, `fish` and `weight_kg`.
:::

## Now you try: press Run yourself

This box adds up all the weights. **Press the ▶ Run button** to see the answer.

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
sum(landings_example$weight_kg)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**What you should see:** `44` — the total weight of all six catches, in kilograms.
:::

## Change one thing, then run again

You do **not** need to understand the instruction below yet — that comes in the next lessons. For now,
just see how easy it is to change an answer.

This box shows only the catches **heavier than 5 kg**. **Change the `5` to `9`**, then press **Run** again.

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
landings_example[landings_example$weight_kg > 5, ]
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Try it:** with `5` you see **four** rows. Change it to `9` and press Run — now you see only the **two**
catches above 9 kg. That is all "coding" is here: small instructions you can change, with the answer
right away.
:::

## This works on YOUR data too

The table above was made up. In the next lessons the table will be **your real landing records** — the
same data you can open in **Data Download**, from your own sites.

Here is a peek. Press **Run** to load the first rows of your data:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Fetch the signed-in user's capped, permission-filtered landings as JSON, reusing the API base URL
// the React app publishes to localStorage (getApiBaseUrl). Same bridge as before: behaves like the
// Data Download tab in dev (-> :3001) and prod (-> /api).
landings_data = {
  const token = localStorage.getItem("authToken");
  if (!token) return [];
  const apiBase = localStorage.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || "/api";
  const res = await fetch(`${apiBase}/data-download/explorer-data`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: "application/json" }
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    console.warn(`explorer-data fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
    return [];
  }
  return await res.json();
}
```

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
#| input:
#|   - landings_data
# quarto-live converts the JS array of row objects into an R data.frame automatically.
landings <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(landings_data), error = function(e) data.frame())

if (nrow(landings) == 0) {
  cat("Your data will appear here once you are signed in to the platform.\n")
} else {
  cat("Loaded", nrow(landings), "of your landing records.\n")
  head(landings)
}
```

## What you will learn next

Each lesson is short and uses your own data. You will learn to answer everyday questions:

- 🔎 **Find the rows you need** — *"Show me only the landings from Vanga."* — *"Only last month."*
- 📋 **Pick the columns you need** — *"I only want the date, the site and the weight."*
- ➕ **Add it up** — *"What is the total catch at each site?"* — *"Which gear catches the most?"*

You will only ever **press Run** and **change small things**. Take the lessons in order.
